resolved_runtime_issue.cause: Original collector candidates are float32. Candidate coordinate addition and area multiplication occur at float32 before their results mix with float64 GT/intersection arithmetic. The original replay compared those stored mixed-precision overlaps to a geometry helper that promoted candidate boxes to float64 before addition and multiplication. The two conventions can differ enough to fail the original1e-5/1e-7 allclose check even for intact accepted arrays.

resolved_runtime_issue.minimal_fix_assessment: collected_iou repeats the original per-frame candidate/GT arithmetic without early candidate promotion and checks all24 stored overlaps with np.array_equal. E0 baseline and selected candidate proposal are separately evaluated through the same float64 box_iou function. This fixes the demonstrated arithmetic mismatch without relaxing tolerance, changing labels, modifying the checkpoint or introducing a fallback.

engineering_assessments.assessment: collected_iou iterates per candidate set, casts each GT row to float64 and leaves accepted candidate dtype unchanged. Its max/min, candidate corner addition, intersection and candidate area expressions match original overlap_labels. Replay now requires exact value equality for the entire stored IoU matrix, strengthening coverage from selected candidates to every24-candidate set. It does not replace or rewrite stored IoUs or labels. Existing accepted NPZ bytes remain the schema/dtype provenance.

Current E0 baseline uses predictions[frame] and same-frame GT. A positive head index maps to candidate chosen-1, whose IoU is freshly computed by the same float64 box_iou helper. Index0 leaves the E0 IoU unchanged. Thus identical candidate/E0 boxes have exactly zero delta rather than an artificial mixed-precision difference, and an identical box/GT pair has IoU1. Cached mixed-precision IoUs are used only for original-data validation, not as the numerical comparison for proposed outcomes.

Head inputs, raw-logit argmax, fixed candidate order and original label indexing are unchanged. No float64 diagnostic IoU is used to relabel positives, choose candidates or alter no-match truth. Exact AST comparisons confirm unchanged classification counter formulas and both-partition saved-metric guards. Holdout2747/3450, candidate2685/3318 and no-match62/132 remain required; fit10765/13074, candidate10238/12281 and no-match527/793 remain bound through checkpoint.metrics. Actual frozen-head reproduction was not performed by this reviewer.

Reliable-to-below-half counts a selected outcome falling below0.5 from a reliable baseline; lost-to-at-least-half counts a selected outcome reaching0.5 from lost.
